name: Terminal Chrome
description: A text console: square corners, rules dashed in the default border color, cards boxed in a double ink line, controls outlined in ink, tight padding, no shadows, stepped motion that cuts instead of easing, a cursor blink for emphasis, and scanlines on the shared surfaces.

provenance.attribution: Keyur Golani, for the keyurgolani.name portfolio platform.
provenance.derivation: The reviewed prototype's terminal recipe, with its --appearance-* references read as --color-*, and the contract's signature-fill and emphasis-glow at the fallback language's values.

fallbacks: Under reduced transparency, without backdrop-filter, in forced colors, and in print, surfaces render opaque and the backdrop blur is 0.
Under reduced motion, transforms and emphasis stop and entrances and exits fade; a paused boundary and print are instant.
In forced colors, the material is a solid surface, and shadows and texture drop.
caveats: Translucent surfaces with a backdrop blur cost paint time on slower devices, and read less clearly over busy content.
A decorative gradient texture sits behind surfaces.
Its scanlines draw in the canvas color, not the prototype's text color, so they sit away from the text and never take contrast from it.

Ships opaque: its approved 92% translucent surfaces fall under the contrast targets with its texture over a black or white backdrop, so its surfaces are 100% opaque, and only a dialog's backdrop is blurred. This supersedes the translucency caveats above.

tokens.surface-material: linear-gradient(color-mix(in srgb, var(--color-surface-default) 92%, transparent), color-mix(in srgb, var(--color-surface-default) 92%, transparent))
tokens.texture: repeating-linear-gradient(0deg, transparent 0 3px, color-mix(in srgb, var(--color-canvas) 10%, transparent) 3px 4px)
